recentItems.title: Xi'an, where the Silk Road meets the screen
recentItems.description:
📺 Subscribe to our YouTube channel and stay updated with our latest analysis and interviews:👇
https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCgrNz-aDmcr2uuto8_DL2jg 👈

Xi'an, the starting point of the ancient Silk Road, is the host city of the 13th Silk Road International Film Festival. Some 2,130 films from 139 countries and regions were submitted this year – the widest reach in the festival's history. And something else is new in 2026: Egypt is the festival's first guest country of honor, in the year China and Egypt mark seven decades of diplomatic ties.

"Our grandfathers in China and Egypt were trying to do their contribution to the world of art and cinema," Egyptian animator Mohamed Ghazala said during an interview with CGTN's Zhang Meng. "That's why we are here in Xi'an – celebrating the Silk Road International Film Festival, which is bringing East and West to talk."

recentItems.title: Exclusive with president of the National Assembly of Angola Adão de Almeida
recentItems.description:
China and Angola are expanding cooperation across trade, investment, technology and other areas. How can this partnership contribute to Angola's economic diversification? What role can China play in supporting Angola's development and talent growth? On Leaders Talk, CMG's Zou Yun spoke with Adão de Almeida, president of the National Assembly of Angola, during his visit to China from September 9 to 16. In this episode, they discuss the evolution of bilateral relations and examine how Chinese companies are contributing to Angola's economic diversification. They also explore China's development path, technological progress and legislative system, and look at China's role in advancing science and technology.

recentItems.title: The China Americans came to love
recentItems.description:
📺 Subscribe to our YouTube channel and stay updated with our latest analysis and interviews:👇
https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCgrNz-aDmcr2uuto8_DL2jg 👈

You may not have noticed, but Americans, especially the younger generation, are falling in love with a "specific" China. As prejudice fades, China is becoming something they can feel and touch: It might be a melody that resonates across the ocean, or the daily habit of soaking goji berries and drinking hot water; it might be the similar memes Chinese and American young people use on social media, or the everyday life of American students studying in China. To them, China is no longer just a phrase in news headlines, but the food they've tasted, the roads they've walked, and the friends they've made. Let's see through their eyes what kind of China they have truly seen.

recentItems.title: Expert: Healthy habits key to chronic disease management
recentItems.description:
📺 Subscribe to our YouTube channel and stay updated with our latest analysis and interviews:👇
https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCgrNz-aDmcr2uuto8_DL2jg 👈

Chronic diseases account for roughly 88% of all deaths in China, but changing the unhealthy habits linked to them remains a major challenge, said Dr. Shao Ruitai, a professor at the School of Population Medicine and Public Health at Peking Union Medical College.

Healthy habits, including a healthy diet, going to bed early and reducing or avoiding smoking, are key to preventing chronic diseases, Shao said in an interview with CGTN's Health Talk on the sidelines of the Boao Forum for Asia Global Health Forum.

Shao called for greater efforts to promote healthy lifestyles and public health knowledge. He also highlighted the potential of AI and wearable devices in disease prevention, early detection and management, while stressing that the use of personal and health data should be based on informed consent and follow proper procedures to protect privacy.

The Boao Forum for Asia Global Health Forum 2026 was held in Haikou from September 15 to 16, with guests from 32 countries and regions attending the event.

recentItems.title: How to care for loved ones with Alzheimer's: Practical advice for family caregivers
recentItems.description:
📺 Subscribe to our YouTube channel and stay updated with our latest analysis and interviews:👇
https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCgrNz-aDmcr2uuto8_DL2jg 👈

Caring for a loved one with Alzheimer's requires patience, empathy and adaptive caregiving strategies. Dr. Zhang Wei, director of the Center for Cognitive Neurology at Beijing Tiantan Hospital, emphasizes that non-pharmacological care is crucial for managing behavioral symptoms. Caregivers should prioritize emotional connection over logic, avoiding pitfalls like arguing over facts or stripping away independence through overprotection. Simple actions – validating feelings, using gentle distraction, and encouraging manageable daily tasks – go a long way in preserving the person's dignity and delaying cognitive decline.
